title: What SMLIGHT already solves — and what it changes for MC1
lead: Current SLZB-xU devices can run the Thread border router locally. Their ESP32-S3, W5500 and separate radio architecture supports our compact-host direction; it does not remove the host processor.
decision: Keep S3-Nano-M as the current full-function candidate. Use SLZB-MRxU as an architecture reference and a possible finished Zigbee/Thread appliance. Prioritize recovery testing before committing the next carrier layout.
scope: Source and compatibility review. No SMLIGHT unit was measured, flashed or tested. The existing MC1 and compact-S3 firmware builds do not establish SMLIGHT hardware parity.

findings.title: The architecture is already used in a finished product
findings.text: MRxU combines an ESP32-S3 host, W5500 Ethernet and two independent radio SoCs. MR5U uses two MG24 radios. The host still owns networking and application services; one radio serves Zigbee and the other Thread.

findings.title: Thread over Ethernet has two different meanings
findings.text: Classic mode sends radio serial traffic to an OTBR process on another machine. The newer on-device mode runs the border router in the SLZB itself and exposes a REST API. Only the latter matches the location of our Thread stack.

findings.title: Native BLE is not our active Bluetooth proxy
findings.text: SLZB-OS on U/Ultima forwards advertisements to Home Assistant and supports scanning, but its manual explicitly excludes active BLE connections. Our full profile retains three active ESPHome BLE connections.

findings.title: Less PSRAM can work, but the workload matters
findings.text: U-series documentation specifies 2 MB PSRAM. That weakens any claim that a local Thread border router inherently needs 8 MB. It does not measure our larger concurrent workload, and the selected Nano keeps 8 MB without adding a component.

findings.title: A Thread failure can restart our entire host
findings.text: Source review of our pinned ESP-IDF/OpenThread path found that fatal RCP reset failure can reach assertion/termination and reboot the S3. The normal returned-error path keeps other services alive, but it does not cover every lower-layer failure. This is a source-identified risk, not a reproduced hardware crash.

modes.name: Classic SLZB + external OTBR
modes.thread: OTBR on HA/Linux; radio stream crosses the network
modes.zigbee: Separate radio required for simultaneous Zigbee
modes.ble: Depends on firmware; do not combine features from different images
modes.extra: A useful remote-radio design, but a different failure boundary

modes.name: SLZB-MRxU / native SLZB-OS
modes.zigbee: Independent second radio; coordinator mode is distinct from Zigbee Hub mode
modes.extra: Finished PoE appliance; USB/add-ons depend on exact model

modes.name: Official SLZB ESPHome profile
modes.thread: Reviewed profile exports radio UARTs; external OTBR required
modes.extra: Replaces the core firmware; not an extra service inside SLZB-OS

modes.name: Our S3-Nano candidate
modes.ble: Three active connections configured and compiled
modes.extra: Z-Wave, CC1101 RF, LD2450 and BME680; hardware concurrency untested

improvements.title: Prove recovery, not just startup
improvements.text: Define a deliberate response to fatal RCP failure: the pinned stack can terminate the host, and registering a no-op callback is not a fix. Then fault-inject a missing/rebooting RCP, Ethernet loss and address renewal. Check IPv6 forwarding, OMR routes, discovery and REST recovery while the other services run. Preserve the existing tested REST 404 behavior.

improvements.title: Measure the actual shared workload
improvements.text: Record minimum internal heap, largest free block, PSRAM usage, task stack margins and UART/SPI service latency during concurrent traffic and OTA. Vendor RAM capacity is evidence of a different workload, not our runtime measurement.

improvements.title: Keep upgrade and network state recoverable
improvements.text: Verify Thread dataset export/import, reboot persistence, OTA health confirmation and fallback. Keep radio-update procedures separate from normal startup; do not turn every connection error into a network reset.

improvements.title: Use an I2C GPIO expander only when it removes more hardware
improvements.text: Ultima places slow reset/BOOT controls on TCA9555. Moving only our H2 reset and BOOT would save two native GPIO, from 21 to 19, but adds a module and an initialization dependency. Nano already fits 21; there is no demonstrated simplification yet.

buy_or_build.title: For a finished Zigbee + Thread appliance
buy_or_build.text: MRxU is a credible option to evaluate instead of manufacturing that part of the project. Preserve the chosen Zigbee host protocol and test local-OTBR firmware on the actual model. This is a change in project scope if the other functions move elsewhere.

buy_or_build.title: For the complete ceiling hub
buy_or_build.text: Ultima gets closer with Z-Wave and RF options, but active BLE and the existing radar/environment/RF interfaces still need proof. Its three native UARTs can already be occupied by two radios and Z-Wave, leaving the radar needing another serial path.
